summary: **Milestones 1 to 9 are done.** Everything drawn for a family, a couple, a flat and a group of friends is built from its drawing and walked through in a browser in light and dark: the six places, the 36 templates that do work, the Today of each kind of circle, Activity with asks, the Sunday summary, export and leaving. The walk-through uses 610 screens per run, as two or more people where something is private. The screens of the link with Journey are built too and are being walked through now. Every open question is in one place: [What it does](01-requirements.md#questions-for-you).
next: Read the questions in “What it does”: seven things only you can do before real people use it, nineteen product decisions, and the calls I made while building.
Run it on your Mac ([docs/08](08-run-locally.md)) and tell me what is wrong.
The build stops when the account's usage limit is reached, as it did three times on 12 Nov. Nothing is lost when that happens; it carries on when you say so.

open.q: Children who use the app themselves
open.a: Children as profiles that a parent looks after are simple. A child under 13 signing in on their own device brings children's privacy rules with it in most countries (Journey is 13 and over). The build plan starts with **profiles only**: anything a child ticks is ticked on a parent's phone, and screen 4.6 becomes what a parent chooses to show. Say so if you want children signing in themselves.

open.q: Reading what you type or say
open.a: “Type it”, Jot, a scanned bill and a school letter all turn loose words into an event, a bill or a list. The build plan does it **by rules on the phone**: private, free, right for dates, amounts, names and shopping, rough on anything free-form, and it always shows its reading for you to correct. An AI service would read better, costs per use, and the words leave the phone. Which do you want?

An iPhone will not keep a notification for ever or take typing inside a widget; an Android phone does more. I drew what each can really do: on iPhone a pinned note you press and hold to type in (it returns after each add), one-tap chips and ticks in widgets, voice, the Action Button and the share sheet. Is that close enough to what you pictured, or should the iPhone side lean harder on one of them?

You chose **Homeport** on 12 Nov. It has had a web search, not a legal check: no family app by that name turned up, and US trademark listings show several HOMEPORT marks, one of them live and one applied for in June 2026 for other software. Have it checked properly, and decide the domain, before the stores. It is one setting if it has to change.

In this draft only the Vault is scrambled so that the service can't read it. Notes, photos and files are private to the people you choose but readable by the service, so that search inside scans, reminders from documents and moments can work. Scrambling everything is possible and switches those off.
Keeping a family's full-size photos and videos costs roughly US$0.75 to 3 a month per family. A free amount with a family plan is the usual answer. The numbers are yours to set.

The build plan builds everything that is drawn, in eleven milestones: circles and sharing, Library, Plan with Jot, Notes, Money, Vault, keepsakes, the other kinds of circle, what ties it together, the links with Journey, then real services and phones. Each can go to a few test circles before the next. Does anything wait for a second version?
Today, Plan, Notes, Library, Money, Vault. Are these the right six, in the right order? Is anything you'd use daily more than one tap away?

Grouping photos by who is in them is powerful and sensitive, most of all with children. On the phone only, off by default, or not at all? The build plan leaves it out: people are tagged by hand, and “every photo she is in” fills from the tags.
Send a booking, a bill or a school letter to the circle's own address and it arrives as an event or a bill. It needs a mail-receiving service that Journey doesn't have. First version, or later?

updates.text: **Milestones 7, 8 and 9 are built and tested.** Fair and fun: whose turn, the piggy bank, secret missions, the Saturday jar, sleeps until, where is it, habit charts. For couples: our story, tucked notes, the anniversary questions, mystery date, both said yes, the fair share. For housemates: the kitty, a fairer split, heads-up, heard in the kitchen, the guest book with its page at the door, everyone who's lived here. For friends: when can everyone (also by link), Secret Santa, where next, the dictionary, predictions, the awards, a goal you walk together. Each kind of circle has its own Today. What is secret stays secret on the other person's phone, and the walk-through checks that as that person. What ties it together: Activity with its filters and asks (allowing one shares the password from your phone), pushes through one outbox that never names what you can't see, the Sunday summary, export, leaving a circle, and deleting the account with “only Homeport, or Journey too”. Two faults the walk-through found on the way were fixed: someone who deleted only Homeport could never come back, and a made-up address said “couldn't read that” in place of “not available”.

**Milestones 5 and 6 are built and tested: Money and the Vault.** Money: bills that repeat with who pays what, reading a bill from its lines, sheets with formulas written as sentences, a row as a card, the loan planner, splitting costs with the fewest payments. Every figure is worked out by the API, so two phones never disagree. The Vault: passwords, cards, IDs, Wi‑Fi and codes scrambled in the app before they leave it; sharing one so someone can use it, see it or change it, once or until a day; the emergency plan with its wait; your Vault key, helpers who can let you back in, and a new phone. The walk-through reads the database as it goes and fails if a password, a key or a passcode is ever there in the clear. Honest limits, also on the screens: Face ID has never run on a phone (a browser uses a passcode), nothing fills a password into other apps yet, no leak check is connected, and the Vault still needs its outside review before real secrets go in. How to run it on your Mac and how to connect the real services are written (docs 08 and 09).

**Milestones 2, 3 and 4 are built and tested: the Library, Plan with Jot, and Notes.** The Library: the wall by day with its years, a moment, the viewer, albums, places, files, a document with its dates, selecting and sharing, storage. Plan: the day's list, the month, events with answers, Type it, reminders with turns and nudges, goals. Jot: the jot bar, what was filed and where, voice (typed in a browser), sharing in, and the widgets, pinned note and Lock Screen written for the phone build. Notes: spaces and folders inside folders, pages made of blocks with live lists, bills and passwords in them, lists that keep working offline and catch up, a page kept as a surprise. With them, the templates gallery and the first ten templates that do work: meal plan, chore wheel, time capsule, and seven keepsakes. What a phone has to do is stood in and says so on the screen: the camera and reading a scan, the microphone, a map, widgets. The walk-through found and fixed several joins between places on the way; one known flaw is left for the next pass: a long list in a browser sometimes reports a harmless layout error.

**Milestone 1 is built and tested.** 24 screens: welcome, sign-in, the setup for each kind of circle, Home with Today, the circle switcher, search, the + sheet, People, a person's page, the audience sheet, a page hidden from one person, guest passes with the guest's own web page, a child's view, You and its settings. The walk-through signs up new people, sets up a family, a couple, a flat and a crew, and checks as a second person that a private page can't be found on Today, in search or by its address until it is shared. 547 app tests and 845 API tests pass. Two faults it found in the API were fixed: a circle with ticked lists could not be deleted, and the web page for Grandma's stories refused its own form.

**The build has started**, on your go-ahead. The app is called **Homeport** everywhere. Done so far: the API's spine (79 tests, among them every way to reach a thing agreeing on who may see it) and the app's foundation from Journey's (225 tests, a walk-through in light and dark).

**The build plan** is written: a new page in this hub and `docs/06-build-plan.md`. Eleven milestones in Journey's way of working (everything on one computer first, real services last), what “done” means for each, how it is tested, six calls for you with the default I'll build, twelve places where the build can't match the drawing, and all 125 screens with their milestone and test level. The hub's build now fails if that list and the screens ever disagree.

**Health is out**, by your decision: the Health place, its eleven screens, and the health details that had crept into other screens (allergies, blood type, vaccination and medical records). The top row is six places again. Two things stayed because they hold no health details: **habit charts** (now in Fair and fun) and **a goal you walk together** (now with the friends' screens, typed in by hand, no link to the phone's health app).

Two decisions from you. **Notes keeps its name**: Lore is gone from every screen. **Health is in the first version**: it now has its own step in the build order, straight after the Vault whose locked storage it uses, and its legal check moves to the top of the next steps.

Three changes you asked for, 37 more screens. **Lore** is the new name for Notes. **Health** (11 screens) is the seventh place, for every circle: who gave the medicine, a sick day written down, the emergency card, moving together, and more. **A circle's kind** now shapes what it gets: two new setup screens, and a full set each for **couples**, **housemates** and **friends** (8 screens apiece: their Home, their templates, three keepsakes, three small rituals).

After your first three comments: 22 more screens. **Jot** (8): widgets, a note pinned in notifications that you type into, voice, the share button, and how each phone's limits are handled. **Keepsakes** (7): Open when…, the birthday interview, Things they said, Same spot every year, Grandma's stories, the good things jar, the doorframe. **Fair and fun** (6): Whose turn?, the piggy bank, secret missions, the Saturday jar, Sleeps until…, Where is it?. Plus *Goodnight from far away* in the Journey group.

First draft: the hub, 75 screens in 13 groups, the design system copied from Journey's Design 2.1, a name shortlist with a switch on every screen, the link with Journey, the requirements, and the answer on sharing a database and a server.
